name: Congenital Hemidysplasia with Ichthyosiform Erythroderma and Limb Defects Syndrome
aliases: Congenital Hemidysplasia Ichthyosiform Erythroderma Limb Defects

criteria.description: Unilateral congenital hemidysplasia affecting skin and underlying tissues
Presence of ichthyosiform erythroderma with sharp midline demarcation
Ipsilateral limb defects including hypoplasia or aplasia of bones
Identification of pathogenic mutations in NSDHL gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of unilateral ichthyosiform erythroderma with ipsilateral hemidysplasia and limb defects
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for NSDHL mutations supports diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral ichthyosiform erythroderma with sharp midline demarcation
searchTerms: one-sided scaly red skin with sharp border
unilateral fish-scale like skin rash
red scaly skin patch on one side

pathognomonic.symptomName: Ipsilateral congenital hemidysplasia involving skin and subcutaneous tissues
searchTerms: one side skin and tissue under skin underdeveloped
skin and fat tissue missing on one side
unilateral skin and subcutaneous tissue loss
underdeveloped or missing limb on one side
one-sided limb small or absent
limb hypoplasia or aplasia on one side
damaged or malformed nails on one side
nail abnormalities on affected side
nail dystrophy on one hand or foot

common.symptomName: Skeletal abnormalities including hypoplasia of ribs or vertebrae
searchTerms: underdeveloped ribs or spine bones
missing or small ribs or vertebrae
skeletal bone abnormalities in chest or spine
hair loss or abnormal hair on one side
one-sided baldness or hair changes
unilateral alopecia or hair defects
slight unevenness of face
mild facial asymmetry
one side of face slightly different

occasional.symptomName: Ipsilateral hypoplasia of internal organs such as kidney or lung
searchTerms: underdeveloped kidney or lung on one side
one-sided internal organ hypoplasia
smaller organs on affected side
brain development delays
neurological problems with delayed milestones
cognitive and motor delays

occasional.symptomName: Ocular anomalies such as strabismus or ptosis
searchTerms: eye muscle problems like crossed eyes or droopy eyelid
strabismus or ptosis
abnormal eye movements or eyelid drooping

rare.symptomName: Cardiovascular malformations ipsilateral to skin lesions
searchTerms: heart and blood vessel defects on same side as skin lesions
one-sided cardiovascular malformations
heart abnormalities next to skin changes

laboratory: Normal routine labs; genetic testing reveals NSDHL gene mutations
imaging: Radiographs showing ipsilateral limb hypoplasia and skeletal abnormalities
Ultrasound or MRI may show ipsilateral organ hypoplasia
genetic: Pathogenic variants in NSDHL gene on X chromosome
other: Skin biopsy shows epidermal hyperplasia with lipid metabolism abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Blistering vesicular rash in neonatal period

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin lesions beyond typical unilateral distribution
Severe limb malformations causing functional impairment
references: Happle R. CHILD syndrome: congenital hemidysplasia with ichthyosiform erythroderma and limb defects. Am J Med Genet. 1980.
